title: On a slow line a message or complaint to the gym can arrive twice
what: When a member sends a question, feedback or complaint and the answer is lost on the way back (the app stops waiting after 30 seconds), the gym has already saved it but the member is told it could not send, with the words still in the box. Tapping Send again makes a second, separate conversation at the desk. The send carries no id the gym could use to spot the repeat, and each repeat also uses up one of the member's 5 new messages a day.
expected: A message sent again after a lost answer is recognised as the same message and saved once, as orders and joins already are.
how_often: on slow or dropping mobile data
fix_line: Give each new message an id kept on the phone until it is confirmed, and have the gym return the saved one when the same id comes again

title: When MettleUp's server fails, the gym message page and find-my-gym tell the member to check their internet
what: On the Message your gym page, any server answer the app does not recognise shows 'Could not send. Check your internet and try again.' On Find my gym with my number, a server that does not answer within 15 seconds shows 'No internet. Connect and try again.' In both cases the member's phone may be online and the fault is on MettleUp's side, so the member keeps checking their own connection.
expected: A server fault says the gym or MettleUp could not be reached right now, separate from a real no-internet message.
fix_line: Use the 'the gym didn't answer' words for server faults and keep 'No internet' for a phone with no connection

title: A failed gym join, order, cancel or shop refresh says try again but keeps no note of why
what: When joining a gym fails, the gym page from an invite link cannot be read, the shop list or My orders cannot refresh, an order cannot be placed or an order cannot be cancelled, the member sees a try-again message, but the app writes no log line at all, even when the cause is a server fault rather than no internet. Other Gym tab screens do log their failures, so these are the gaps. Nobody can later tell why a member could not join their gym.
expected: Every failure that shows a try-again message writes a short log line with the reason, at least when it is not plain no-internet.
who: members, and MettleUp when helping them
fix_line: Add one log line with the error kind to each of these failure paths
